facts.statement: The fossil was collected in the 1980s from the Calcaire à Bélemnites Formation in Normandy, France, dating to about 185-183 million years ago.
facts.quote: It was collected in the 1980s from the Calcaire à Bélemnites Formation of Normandy, dating to the latest Pliensbachian stage of the late Early Jurassic, about 185-183 million years ago.

facts.statement: The specimen was found in the Roche-Blain quarry near the city of Laize-la-Ville, south of Caen.
facts.quote: It was found in the Roche-Blain quarry, located in the commune of Fresney-le-Puceux near the city of Laize-la-Ville, south of Caen.

facts.statement: The genus is known only from the holotype MAE 2007.1.1(J), which consists of a partial skull, an articulated mandible, and ten associated vertebrae.
facts.quote: Cryonectes is known only from the holotype MAE 2007.1.1(J), a partial skull and articulated mandible, and ten associated vertebrae.

facts.statement: Cryonectes is a moderate-sized pliosaurid with a skull length of 47 cm.
facts.quote: Cryonectes is a moderate-sized pliosaurid, as its skull has a length of 47 cm.

facts.statement: Cryonectes is characterized by a slightly constricted snout, a greatly elongated snout, and a long mandibular symphysis with seven tooth positions and a ventral ridge.
facts.quote: Cryonectes is characterized by a unique combination of characters including a very slight constriction between premaxillae and maxillae, its snout is greatly elongated and the mandible has a long symphysis bearing seven tooth position and retaining a ventral mandibular ridge.

facts.statement: Evidence suggests the specimen was a subadult individual at a relatively early stage of development.
facts.quote: Therefore, Cryonectes is at a relatively early stage in ontogenetic development. The ninth vertebra suggests that it was probably a subadult individual.

facts.statement: Cladistic analysis places Cryonectes as basal to Pliosaurus, Peloneustes, and other pliosaurids.
facts.quote: A cladistic analysis performed by Peggy Vincent, Nathalie Bardet and Emanuela Mattioli found it to be basal to Pliosaurus, Peloneustes and other pliosaurids.

facts.statement: The genus was named by Peggy Vincent, Nathalie Bardet, and Emanuela Mattioli in 2012, with Cryonectes neustriacus as the type species.
facts.quote: Cryonectes was first named by Peggy Vincent, Nathalie Bardet and Emanuela Mattioli in 2012 and the type species is Cryonectes neustriacus.

facts.statement: The genus name Cryonectes means "cold swimmer," referencing the cool climate of the uppermost Pliensbachian period.
facts.quote: The generic name is derived from kryos, Greek for "cold", and nektris (nektes), for "swimmer", and refers to the cool climatic conditions that prevailed during the uppermost Pliensbachian.

facts.statement: The species name neustriacus refers to the Frank kingdom of Neustria in northwest France.
facts.quote: The specific name is derived from the Frank kingdom of Neustrie which covered northwest France, created after the death of Clovis I.

facts.statement: Cryonectes lived during the Early Jurassic period, specifically the upper Pliensbachian stage.
facts.quote: Cryonectes es un género extinto de reptiles saurópsidos pliosauroides que vivieron en el período Jurásico inferior (Pliensbachiano superior).

facts.statement: The time range for Cryonectes is estimated between 192.9 and 184.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Pliensbachian to Pliensbachian (192.9 to 184.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: Cryonectes is classified within the family Pliosauridae.
The authority for the genus Cryonectes is listed as Vincent, Bardet & Mattioli, 2013.
